title: 2014 HMMT February Algebra Problem 1
statement: Given that \(x\) and \(y\) are nonzero real numbers such that \(x+\frac{1}{y}=10\) and \(y+\frac{1}{x}=\frac{5}{12}\), find all possible values of \(x\).

solutions.text:
4,6 OR 6,4 Let \(z=\frac{1}{y}\). Then \(x+z=10\) and \(\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{z}=\frac{5}{12}\). Since \(\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{z}=\frac{x+z}{x z}=\frac{10}{x z}\), we have \(x z=24\). Thus, \(x(10-x)=24\), so \(x^{2}-10 x+24=(x-6)(x-4)=0\), whence \(x=6\) or \(x=4\).

Alternate solution: Clearing denominators gives \(x y+1=10 y\) and \(y x+1=\frac{5}{12} x\), so \(x=24 y\). Thus we want to find all real (nonzero) \(x\) such that \(\frac{x^{2}}{24}+1=\frac{5}{12} x\) (and for any such \(x, y=x / 24\) will satisfy the original system of equations). This factors as \((x-4)(x-6)=0\), so precisely \(x=4,6\) work.
